meta.title: The ten validation gates — pre-registered tests every strategy must pass
meta.note: The gate IDs and thresholds are copied from the root project's data/derived/leaderboard.json and pages/validation.html so the two sites cannot disagree about what a gate is. The 'why' column is this session's explanation, and each row links the statistical authority for the test.

gates.name: Sample size
gates.test: Count settled bets in the evaluation window.
gates.pass_rule: At least 300 settled bets; the luck page's own power table says 9,806 bets are needed to detect a 52% win rate at 80% power.
gates.why: A 137-bet strategy cannot distinguish skill from noise. The gate threshold is a floor, not a sufficiency claim.

gates.name: Significance
gates.test: Two-sided test of the strategy's mean return against zero.
gates.why: The conventional bar; meaningless alone because it is applied many times in one batch.

gates.name: Multiple testing
gates.test: Benjamini-Hochberg across every strategy tested in the batch.
gates.why: Trying more strategies raises the chance the best one looks good by luck. The correction is what makes the leaderboard a competition rather than a search.

gates.name: Positive after vig
gates.test: Bootstrap interval on ROI at the stored prices.
gates.pass_rule: ROI > 0 and the 95% interval excludes zero.
gates.why: An edge must survive the price actually paid, not a fair-odds assumption.

gates.name: Luck permutation
gates.test: Thousands of random portfolios of the same size at the same prices.
gates.pass_rule: The candidate beats at least 95% of them.
gates.why: Directly prices the 'could this be luck' question instead of arguing about it.

gates.name: Track-record length
gates.test: Number of settled bets against the effect size that would be detectable at that n.
gates.pass_rule: Enough bets for the observed effect to be distinguishable from zero.
gates.why: Stops a small, precisely-measured but tiny effect from being promoted.

gates.name: Correlation validity
gates.test: Same-game legs priced with a measured dependence structure rather than independence.
gates.pass_rule: The dependence model is estimated from data and validated out of sample.
gates.why: Independent pricing of correlated legs overstates the payout and inflates apparent value. Measured here: four-leg joint 11.1% vs 5.7% under independence.

gates.name: Temporal stability
gates.test: Develop / validate / holdout split; holdout touched once.
gates.pass_rule: The effect holds in the untouched window.
gates.why: A strategy fitted to one season's quirks is not a strategy.

gates.name: Executable price
gates.test: A price the strategy could actually have taken, with a timestamp and a limit.
gates.pass_rule: The bet is profitable at both the recorded price and a plausible worse price.
gates.why: The single gate that stops everything else: no timestamped price exists in this repository, so every candidate fails here by construction.

gates.name: Independent re-check
gates.test: A second implementation reproduces the result from committed inputs.
gates.why: An unreproducible number cannot be reviewed. This session's audit script is an example of the mechanism.
